title: TensorBoard Embedding Projector — see what word vectors really associate
summary: Uses the TensorBoard Embedding Projector to explore a word2vec model's neighborhoods: 'cold' pulls in Soviet and war, 'sexy' pulls in Groucho and wigs. A quick, visual way to show how embeddings absorb history and cultural bias from training text.
takeaways: Load any embedding model into the Projector to inspect nearest neighbors interactively
Embeddings encode historical and cultural associations, not just definitions — useful for teaching bias

title: Runway Gen-3 — hands-on first test of public text-to-video
summary: A quick paid-tier test of Runway Gen-3 Alpha right after public release: a hyper-real macro prompt (miniature horned puppies on a fingertip, then butterfly wings) took a few generations to land. Mostly a first-impressions reaction, not a workflow.
takeaways: Gen-3 needs several generations per prompt; budget credits accordingly
Macro/close-up subjects with one surreal detail are a reliable showcase prompt style

title: Kimi K2 in an agentic coding class — open models now viable for web apps
summary: Liz the Developer reports her agentic software-development class switched to open-source models (Kimi K2) after Claude token cuts, and the class still shipped a 'Minecraft in space' web game. Light on detail — mostly a vibe check that open models can keep up for web-app builds.
takeaways: Open-weight models like Kimi K2 can replace a paid Claude subscription for classroom-scale web-app builds

title: Five Claude MCP servers — search, browser, docs, tasks, file-to-markdown
summary: A shortlist of MCP servers that give Claude real capabilities: Tavily (LLM-ready search), Playwright (browser automation), Context7 (current library docs, fewer hallucinated APIs), Task Master AI (PRD to dependency-ordered tasks) and Markdownify (PDF/image/audio to markdown). Skills teach Claude how; MCP servers give it access.
takeaways: Context7 cuts deprecated/hallucinated API suggestions by injecting live docs
Task Master AI turns a PRD into an ordered task list Claude can execute step by step
Markdownify lets you feed PDFs, images and audio into any Claude workflow

title: Claude Code agent teams — parallel sessions that message each other
summary: Claude Code's agent teams let separate Claude sessions talk laterally through a shared mailbox, unlike subagents which only report back a single result at the end. It ships disabled; you enable it with an experimental environment variable set to 1 in .claude/settings.json (paid plans only).
takeaways: Agent teams allow agent-to-agent messaging mid-task; subagents cannot coordinate
Enable via the experimental agent-teams env var in settings.json
Use for parallel work where agents must share findings, not just fan-out/fan-in

title: Prompt engineering crash course — local models, system prompts, context engineering
summary: A rapid-fire primer: run a 7–14B model quantized to 4 bits locally (e.g. on a 16 GB Orange Pi), set a system prompt that bans sycophancy and demands citations, add tool use, and save workflows. Argues, citing 12-Factor Agents, that you should own your context engineering rather than lean on frameworks like LangGraph or the OpenAI Agents SDK.
takeaways: A 16 GB single-board computer can run a 4-bit 7B–14B model locally
Put anti-sycophancy and cite-your-sources rules in the system prompt
Build your own agent loop via context engineering instead of adopting a heavy framework

title: ChatGPT 'God Mode' prompt stacking — DM-bait with no content

title: Gemini 2.5 Pro — one-prompt interactive particle visualizer in a single HTML file
summary: Prompt Gemini 2.5 Pro to 'create a particle cloud visualizer that can change shape, color and other properties, interactive, in a single HTML file', answer its clarifying questions, then save the code as .html and open it in a browser. A beginner-friendly vibe-coding recipe for instant creative-coding toys.
takeaways: Ask for 'a single HTML file' to get something you can run with zero setup
If output is malformed, just say 'did not work, remake it'

title: n8n + Veo 3 — Telegram-triggered AI vlog that auto-posts to YouTube
summary: An n8n automation where a Telegram message ('Bigfoot builds a log cabin vlog') becomes an eight-part story, each part rendered with Google Veo 3, stitched together and uploaded to YouTube automatically. Demo only; the guide is behind a comment-for-link.
takeaways: Chain story generation → per-scene video gen → concat → upload in one n8n flow
Telegram makes a convenient trigger for content pipelines

title: Three Claude Code repos — CLI-Anything, GSD 2 and Garry Tan's gstack
summary: CLI-Anything (from the LightRAG team) points Claude Code at any open-source app and generates a CLI for it, riding the shift from MCPs to CLIs. GSD 2 turns the Get Shit Done framework into a standalone CLI on the Pi SDK, and gstack is YC CEO Garry Tan's personal Claude Code setup.
takeaways: CLI-Anything can wrap any OSS tool as a CLI your agent can drive
GSD 2 runs outside Claude Code but won't (safely) use a Claude Max plan
Study gstack for a real operator's Claude Code configuration

title: Ten Claude Code plugins and CLIs — databases, deploys, scraping, diagrams
summary: A practical kit: Supabase CLI, Anthropic's skill-creator (create, test and benchmark skills), GSD orchestration, notebooklm-py, Obsidian vaults, Vercel CLI, Playwright CLI, GitHub CLI, Firecrawl CLI/skill for scraping, and an Excalidraw diagram skill. The theme: CLI tools beat MCPs for coding agents.
takeaways: Use skill-creator to benchmark and evaluate your existing skills, not just write new ones
Pair GitHub CLI + Vercel CLI for push-to-deploy entirely from Claude Code
Run Claude Code inside an Obsidian vault for a markdown-native personal assistant

title: RAG-Anything + LightRAG — multimodal graph RAG for images, charts and docs
summary: LightRAG builds knowledge-graph RAG but only ingests text; pairing it with RAG-Anything adds images, charts, graphs and other non-text documents. The combo runs fully local or cheaply and plugs into Claude Code.
takeaways: RAG-Anything fills LightRAG's text-only ingestion gap
Both can run locally for near-zero inference cost

title: Karpathy-style LLM knowledge base — Claude Code turns 36 videos into a linked wiki
summary: Following Andrej Karpathy's viral post on LLM-maintained knowledge bases, Claude Code ingested 36 YouTube videos, extracted tools, techniques and skills, and built an interlinked graph of documents (hubs like 'Claude Code' linking to Playwright, browser automation, ClickUp) with summaries and source links.
takeaways: Paste Karpathy's post into Claude Code and ask it to replicate the system on your own corpus
Have the agent extract tools/techniques per source so hubs emerge naturally
Keep source links in each node so the wiki stays verifiable

title: LightRAG + Claude Code — graph RAG over thousands of docs, exposed as skills
summary: LightRAG extracts entities and relationships into a knowledge graph so Claude Code can answer across thousands of documents beyond its context window. Setup: Docker, give Claude Code the LightRAG URL and ask it to install; then have Claude turn the LightRAG server API endpoints into skills for direct querying.
takeaways: Let Claude Code install LightRAG itself from the repo URL
Convert LightRAG's REST endpoints into Claude Code skills for one-line querying
Graph RAG scales retrieval far beyond the context window and can run fully local

title: Recursive Language Models (RLM) — Hindi explainer on beating context limits
summary: A Hindi-language explainer of the Recursive Language Models paper, which lets an LLM treat a long prompt as a variable it can inspect and recursively query instead of stuffing it into context. The transcript is badly garbled, so detail beyond the core idea is unrecoverable.
takeaways: RLMs recurse over prompt chunks as an alternative to RAG or bigger context windows

title: Claude Code content system — seven skills from research to repurposing
summary: Chase's creator pipeline as seven Claude Code skills: source research (X, GitHub), a YT-pipeline skill offloading analysis to NotebookLM, competitive ideation, hook/outline/title scripting, and post-production repurposing into blogs, X threads and 60–120s shorts. Credited with 90 pieces in 30 days; the skills themselves are paywalled.
takeaways: Offload heavy research analysis to NotebookLM to save tokens
Split the pipeline into research → ideation → scripting → repurposing skills
Distill long videos into new short-form scripts rather than clipping

title: Five new Claude Code repos — autoresearch, OpenSpace, CLI-Anything, peers, gws
summary: Karpathy's autoresearch runs continuous keep-or-revert experiments against a measurable target (83 runs, 15 kept); OpenSpace auto-fixes, improves and learns skills from real usage; CLI-Anything wraps apps like GIMP, Blender and Inkscape as CLIs; claude-peers lets separate Claude Code sessions talk; gws is a Google Workspace CLI.
takeaways: autoresearch only works on targets with a binary improved/not-improved metric (e.g. speed)
Use claude-peers for generator + evaluator sessions with instant feedback
gws gives Claude Code full Google Workspace access from the terminal

title: Claude Code source leak — npm debug bundle, mass forks and a Python rewrite
summary: A retelling of the Claude Code leak: a ~60 MB debug/source file shipped inside an npm update, was spotted within minutes, forked tens of thousands of times despite DMCA takedowns, rewritten in Python by a heavy-user developer in hours (a record-fast star count) and mirrored to a decentralized host. Irony noted: the leak included an 'undercover mode' meant to stop Claude leaking internals.
takeaways: Audit published npm packages for source maps and debug artifacts before release
Once code is forked and mirrored, takedowns can't recall it

title: Animated UI component library site — copy-paste timers, buttons and effects

takeaways: Useful category, but you'll need to find the site yourself — it's not named

title: John Cleese on extremism — why having enemies feels so good (1987)
summary: Cleese's 1987 satirical monologue: extremism's appeal is that it supplies a ready-made list of enemies so you can project all badness outward — and both hard left and hard right lists end with 'moderates'. A sharp, quotable case for nuance and critical thinking.
takeaways: Polarization works by offering moral license via an enemy list
Both extremes share one enemy: moderates

title: Bas-relief panel detailing — handmade sculptural wall art in progress
summary: Silent process clip from a St. Petersburg bas-relief studio refining details on a sculpted wall picture for interior design. Visual reference only; no technique narration.
takeaways: Reference for relief texture and interior wall-art finishing

title: Escher's Print Gallery — 3Blue1Brown on the complex-analysis loop at its center
summary: 3Blue1Brown's 45-minute visual deep dive on M.C. Escher's 1956 lithograph Print Gallery, building on de Smit and Lenstra's 2003 analysis that reveals the self-similar conformal loop and answers what belongs in the picture's blank center.
takeaways: Print Gallery's warp is a conformal (complex-analysis) map with a self-similar loop
De Smit and Lenstra's analysis fills in Escher's blank center
Great reference for recursive/Droste visual effects

title: Samurai Jack color design — the 60:30:10 rule in wide landscape shots
summary: Breakdown of how Genndy Tartakovsky's Samurai Jack tells story through visuals, applying the 60:30:10 color rule (dominant, secondary, accent) to vast landscape wides that convey the scale of Jack's journey. Drawn from traditional art rather than cartoon convention.
takeaways: Split a frame into 60% dominant, 30% secondary, 10% accent color
Use wide shots plus restrained palettes to sell scale

title: Daniel de Bruin mirror systems — kinetic mechanical sculpture test
summary: Silent test footage of new mirror mechanisms from engineer-artist Daniel de Bruin (with Heleen Blanken) — a kinetic, mechanically driven light/mirror art piece. Inspiration reference without build detail.
takeaways: Mirror-based kinetic mechanisms as an installation idea
